Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test of K-1 against K classes (Mplus TECH11)

lmr.Rd

Likelihood-ratio test of the fitted K-class model against a model with one class fewer, with the reference distribution of Vuong (1989) for non-nested models as adapted to mixtures by Lo, Mendell & Rubin (2001), and the Lo-Mendell-Rubin adjusted statistic.

Usage

lmr(object)

Arguments

object

A fitted latentmix model with K >= 2 classes and no covariates.

Value

An object of class c("latentmix_lmr", "latentmix_aux"), a list with h0_ll (log-likelihood of the K-1 class model), lr (2 times the log-likelihood difference), df (difference in free parameters), mean, sd (of the Vuong reference distribution), p (VLMR p-value), lr_adjusted, p_adjusted (adjusted LMR test), K and text.

Details

The K-1 class model is re-estimated from the K-class solution with one class deleted (Mplus deletes its first class; here the best of the K deletions is kept). The adjusted statistic is \(LR / (1 + 1/((p_1 - p_0)\log n))\).

The H0 log-likelihood, the likelihood-ratio statistic, the difference in parameters and the adjusted statistic agree with Mplus TECH11, but the p-values can differ from Mplus: they follow Vuong (1989) and Lo, Mendell & Rubin (2001) as published, whereas Mplus does not document its computation. Not available for models with covariates. Simulation studies favour the bootstrap test (blrt()) for class enumeration (Nylund, Asparouhov & Muthén 2007).

References

Vuong, Q. H. (1989). Likelihood ratio tests for model selection and non-nested hypotheses. Econometrica, 57(2), 307–333. doi:10.2307/1912557

Lo, Y., Mendell, N. R., & Rubin, D. B. (2001). Testing the number of components in a normal mixture. Biometrika, 88(3), 767–778. doi:10.1093/biomet/88.3.767

Nylund, K. L., Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. O. (2007). Deciding on the number of classes in latent class analysis and growth mixture modeling: A Monte Carlo simulation study. Structural Equation Modeling, 14(4), 535–569. doi:10.1080/10705510701575396

See also

blrt(), fittable(), lm_table() (lmr argument of the fit comparison).

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# How many ACE classes? Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test of K - 1 against K classes
m4 <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
m5 <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 5)
lmr(m4)   # small p: four classes fit better than three
#> ━━ Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test: 3 vs. 4 classes ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   H0 log-likelihood (K - 1 classes)  -5316.153
#>   2 × LL difference                    136.292
#>   Difference in parameters                   9
#>   VLMR p                                <0.001
#>   Adjusted LMR LRT                     134.253
#>   Adjusted LMR p                        <0.001
lmr(m5)   # p > 0.05: a fifth class is not needed (the data were generated with four)
#> ━━ Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test: 4 vs. 5 classes ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   H0 log-likelihood (K - 1 classes)  -5248.007
#>   2 × LL difference                     15.454
#>   Difference in parameters                   9
#>   VLMR p                                 0.111
#>   Adjusted LMR LRT                      15.223
#>   Adjusted LMR p                         0.116
# }
